lw02.reasoning: The goal asks for two things: recall the season's concrete results and connect them to the modest request. Option 0 does both: a robot that couldn't turn left, a ninth-place finish, donated parts and a small investment. Option 1 is a polite sign-off but mentions no results and says nothing about the request.

Option 3 is the only version that ties to all three named values: steady attendance (participation), new skills (learning) and very little money (careful use of money). Option 0 is a promise to win, not evidence, and it touches none of those values.
Option 0 is the only version that links the report to the budget vote. Option 1 gives no reason the report matters to the decision, and its second clause undercuts the report.

Option 1 makes an arguable claim and previews build, learning and needs in paragraph order. Option 3 is only an announcement of topics, not a claim the report must prove, and it lists the competition instead of next year's needs.

Option 3 draws a reasonable inference: steady attendance shows commitment, which justifies funding. Option 1 makes an unsupported prediction ('certainly' more than twenty members) and never connects the attendance to the funding claim.

Option 3 admits the inexperience plainly, in measured language, and keeps the focus on building a robot. Option 0 is formal, but it hedges instead of admitting and shifts the subject to 'engineering ideas.'

lw05.reasoning: Option [1] puts the flood at the center instead of the marsh, and it leaves no field for 'it' in sentence 2 to refer to. Option [0] ties the field to the route students take to school and keeps the field as the referent.

Option [0] uses the passage's own figures: 180,000 is about three times 64,000, so the comparison speaks directly to taxpayer cost. Option [1] claims savings on mowing, road salt and school supplies, and nothing in the passage supports any of them.
Option [0] previews only the flooding benefit. Option [1] takes a clear position and names all three benefits in the order the editorial discusses them.
Option [0] explains why the field is dry but does not apply the sponge comparison to the April flood. Option [2] makes that connection directly.
'Despite' signals contrast, not addition. 'Beyond' presents the lab as one more benefit, which is what the stem asks for.

Option [0] misplaces its modifying clauses, so it reads awkwardly and is unclear. Option [2] is clear, concise and grammatical, and it keeps both the location and the fact that the field was once a marsh.
